paragraphs.text: A cake of [ripe pu’er](shou:definition) from Yiwu, in Yunnan. The leaf was sun dried, then wetted and heaped in a [fermenting pile](shou:wet-piling) that was turned as it warmed and held below about 65°C for a month or two. After that it was dried and pressed, so the tea is ready to drink now rather than after years of keeping.

brewing.text: Ease a piece off the cake along its edge with a pick rather than snapping it. Use boiling water, about 7 grams to 100 ml, one quick rinse, then short steeps that lengthen as the leaf opens. Ripe tea forgives a heavy hand and gives eight or more good cups.

notice.text: A smooth, sweet cup with earthy or woody notes, and in a young ripe tea a faint smell of the pile that fades with airing or in the first steeps.
